key: If the age was unsuitable and their mission at failure, they fell back upon their own resources and waited.
s: The chapter says the retired scholars did not hide but met an unsuited age; Guo Xiang, on 16.27, reads the waiting as a sage’s calm in a busy age: rooted deep, he waits for things to act of themselves, so the Way is not lost.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 16, on 16.27, zh.wikisource (Nanhua zhenjing zhushu, juan 18, Zhengtong Daozang), revision 6365330 (2026)

evidence.words: 雖有事之世，而聖人未始不澹漠也，故深根寧極而待其自為耳，斯道之所以不喪也。
evidence.gloss: Even in an age given to affairs, the sage is never other than calm and still; so he roots himself deep, rests in the utmost, and waits for things to act of themselves; this is how the Way is not lost.

reason: Problem holds: ‘blaming the times’ dangles and can be read as the scholars blaming the times, while day.js 16.27 has the chapter say it was that the age was not suitable for their mission. The suggested plain sense brought the sentence to 50 words (entry-check refused it), so it is cut to 14 words, ‘The chapter says the retired scholars did not hide but met an unsuited age’, which keeps the fix’s sense in the text’s own terms and repeats no four words of the key.
